name: Spring Boot + Kotlin
description: Best practices for Spring Boot applications written in Kotlin

rules.title: Use layered architecture
rules.content: Organise code into Controller → Service → Repository layers. Controllers must not contain business logic. Services must not depend on HTTP request/response objects.

rules.title: Prefer data classes for DTOs
rules.content: Use Kotlin data classes for all request/response DTOs. Avoid using Map<String, Any> as a return type.

rules.title: Use constructor injection
rules.content: Inject dependencies via primary constructor. Do not use field injection (@Autowired on fields).

rules.title: Use @SpringBootTest sparingly
rules.content: Prefer @WebMvcTest for controller tests and Mockito/MockK for unit tests. Reserve @SpringBootTest for integration tests only.

rules.title: Never log sensitive data
rules.content: Do not log passwords, tokens, or PII. Use structured logging (logback) and mask sensitive fields.

rules.title: Follow Spring naming conventions
rules.content: Suffix classes with their role: UserController, UserService, UserRepository. Use camelCase for function names.
